__acad.Met een aandeel word je mede-eigenaar va: With a share you become a co-owner of a company. If the company earns more, the share usually becomes worth more. Some companies pay part of their profit to shareholders: that is called a dividend.
__acad.Aandelen worden verhandeld op een beurs,: Shares are traded on an exchange, such as Euronext in Amsterdam or the NYSE and Nasdaq in New York. The price comes from supply and demand: if more people want to buy than sell, the price rises.
__acad.Een beurs is niet altijd open. Euronext: An exchange is not always open. Euronext Amsterdam trades on weekdays from 09:00 to 17:30. The US exchanges are open from 15:30 to 22:00 Dutch time. Crypto, on the other hand, trades 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
__acad.Nieuws dat buiten de handelstijden uitko: News that comes out outside trading hours often shows up as a price jump at the open.
__acad.Een index volgt een mandje aandelen, zoa: An index follows a basket of stocks, such as the AEX (25 large Dutch companies) or the S&P 500 (500 large US companies). An ETF is a fund you buy as a single share that follows such an index. It spreads your money over many companies in one go.
__acad.Een aandeel is een deel van een bedrijf;: A share is a part of a company; the price follows supply and demand.
__acad.Beurzen hebben vaste handelstijden; cryp: Exchanges have fixed trading hours; crypto always trades.
__acad.Met een ETF koop je in één keer een hele: With an ETF you buy an entire index in one go.

__acad.Dividend is het deel van de winst dat ee: A dividend is the part of the profit that a company pays out to its shareholders.

__acad.De NYSE en Nasdaq openen om 9:30 lokale: The NYSE and Nasdaq open at 9:30 local time, which is 15:30 in the Netherlands, and close at 22:00 Dutch time.
__acad.Wat doet een ETF die de S&P 500 volgt?: What does an ETF that tracks the S&P 500 do?
__acad.Hij belegt in één Amerikaans bedrijf: It invests in one US company
__acad.Hij volgt de 500 grote Amerikaanse bedri: It follows the 500 large US companies in the index
__acad.Een index-ETF koopt de bedrijven uit de: An index ETF buys the companies in the index, so with one purchase you spread over all of them.
__acad.Bij een exchange (handelsplatform) bewaa: On an exchange (trading platform), the platform holds your crypto for you. That is convenient, but you trust that the platform is secure and solvent. With your own wallet you keep the keys yourself.
__acad.Een eigen wallet geeft je een herstelzin: Your own wallet gives you a recovery phrase (seed phrase) of 12 or 24 words. Whoever has those words has your crypto. Write them down on paper, keep them safe and never share them with anyone.
__acad.Geen enkele echte helpdesk vraagt ooit o: No real helpdesk will ever ask for your recovery phrase. Anyone who does is a scammer.
__acad.Gebruik een uniek, lang wachtwoord per p: Use a unique, long password for each platform.
__acad.Zet tweestapsverificatie aan met een aut: Turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, not via SMS.
__acad.Controleer altijd het webadres voordat j: Always check the web address before you log in; fake sites often look exactly like the original.
__acad.Klik niet op links in onverwachte mails: Don't click links in unexpected emails or messages about your account.
__acad.Een hardware wallet is een klein apparaa: A hardware wallet is a small device that keeps your keys offline. It is the safest way to hold amounts you want to keep for a long time. For active trading, most people keep part of their funds on a reliable exchange.
__acad.Op een exchange bewaart het platform je: On an exchange the platform holds your crypto; in your own wallet you do that yourself.
__acad.Je herstelzin is je crypto: deel hem noo: Your recovery phrase is your crypto: never share it.
__acad.Tweestapsverificatie met een app is een: Two-factor authentication with an app is the minimum security.

__acad.Een hardware wallet bewaart je sleutels: A hardware wallet keeps your keys offline. That is ideal for long-term storage, but less convenient for daily trading.
__acad.Bijna elk platform rekent een vergoeding: Almost every platform charges a fee per transaction, often a percentage of the amount, such as 0.15% to 0.25%. On a purchase of €1,000 you then pay €1.50 to €2.50. When you sell, you pay again.
__acad.De spread is het verschil tussen de hoog: The spread is the difference between the highest bid price and the lowest ask price. If you buy instantly (a market order), you pay the ask price. For coins with little trading the spread can be large.
__acad.Slippage ontstaat als je order groter is: Slippage happens when your order is larger than what is available at the best price. Part of it is then filled at a worse price. A limit order prevents that: you set the maximum price yourself.
__acad.Wie vaak handelt, betaalt vaak. Twee tra: If you trade often, you pay often. Two trades a day at 0.25% per transaction can easily cost you more than your entire deposit over a year. Calculate it yourself below.
__acad.Kosten worden bij aan- én verkoop gereke: Fees are charged on both buying and selling.
__acad.Spread en slippage zijn verborgen kosten: Spread and slippage are hidden costs; limit orders help you keep them down.
__acad.Hoe vaker je handelt, hoe zwaarder koste: The more often you trade, the more fees weigh.

__acad.De spread is het verschil tussen wat kop: The spread is the difference between what buyers bid and what sellers ask.
__acad.Met een limietorder stel je zelf de prij: With a limit order you set the price yourself: the maximum you pay when buying or the minimum you accept when selling.

__acad.Een stijgende trend herken je aan hogere: You recognise an uptrend by higher highs and higher lows: every pullback stops higher than the previous one. In a downtrend it's the other way round: lower highs and lower lows. In between is a sideways market without a clear direction.
__acad.Een voortschrijdend gemiddelde (SMA) mid: A moving average (SMA) averages the closing prices of the last days. If the price is above the 20- and 50-day averages, and the 20-day average is above the 50-day, the short-term trend is up.
__acad.Kruist een korter gemiddelde een langer: When a shorter average crosses above a longer one, traders call it a golden cross; crossing below is called a death cross. They are signals after the fact, not predictions.
__acad.Veel traders handelen liever met de tren: Many traders prefer to trade with the trend rather than against it. A trend can last a long time, but it can also break suddenly. That's why you always combine a trend with a plan for when things go wrong.
